method.title: How to read these comparisons
method.selection: The latest 5 or 10 completed DC sessions are selected by start time. Sessions with missing measurements remain in the selection, so gaps in your history are visible.
method.timing: 10–80% time is the elapsed time between reaching 10% and 80%. Thresholds use recorded timestamps or linear interpolation between adjacent readings no more than two minutes apart. Missing ranges are never extrapolated.
method.power: Observed average power weights continuous measurements by elapsed time across the whole session. Coverage shows how much of the session duration was observed. Peak power is the highest valid recorded session peak or measurement; it may exist even without a curve.
method.median: The median is the middle value of the available results. Average-power comparisons can cover different battery ranges; compare the curves at the same state of charge for context.
method.slow: A slower-session hint requires at least three other complete 10–80% timings, and a duration at least 25% and five minutes above their median. No hint means these conditions were not met; it does not establish normal performance.
method.temperature: Outside temperature is not battery temperature. Temperature matching is used only when at least three other complete timings have average outside temperatures within 5 °C. It cannot show whether cold weather caused slower charging.
